newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour urges Tory candidate to stand down.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour urges Tory candidate to stand down.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said on Sunday that the Conservative candidate for Lincoln should stand down following allegations of a scheme to siphon votes away from Labour in his marginal seat.
"The revelation that the candidate was aware of the scheme makes it essential that he stands down," Brian Wilson, Labour's campaign spokemsan, said in a statement.
He urged the ruling Conservatives to "make a clear statement on the candidate's position and whether the same trick is being played in other marginal seats."

His statement followed a report in the Observer newspaper that a Conservative election agent had secretly plotted to finance a Green Party candidate to strip votes from Labour in the marginal Lincoln seat.
In a taped conversation last week, the agent promised to send a cash-filled envelope to pay the candidate's deposit, said the paper.

"An Observer investigation can reveal that Robin Meads, a Tory agent and constituency chairman, arranged the undercover payment to persuade the Greens to field a candidate in the closely contested seat of Lincoln. Yesterday he resigned after he was confronted with our evidence," said the paper.
Lincoln is the 15th most marginal Conservative seat.
The Conservative candidate Tony Brown was quoted by the paper as saying he knew about his agent's scheme.
"I was aware that he had been having discussions with the Green Party although I was not aware of the detail," the paper quoted him as saying. "It was not my idea."

The Conservatives struggled to shake off sleaze allegations at the outset of their campaign to win power in the May 1 election, with the so-called cash-for-questions scandal and allegations of sexual wrongdoing swamping the political agenda.
